author: marici.Strominger

checks.statement: the branch coefficient factors into three linear characters
the reflected numerator difference is 2q times that character
branch antisymmetrization cancels both magnetic denominators
the branch-difference identity holds grade by grade
the branch sum is twice the neutral transported column
the two-branch exterior character contains the scalar 2q
branch diagonalization degenerates exactly at q=0
adding quadratic branch dependence destroys affine diagonalization

verdict: The transported numerator is affine in the reflection-branch parameter s, with coefficient (1+x)(1+t)(1-xt). Hence B_(+q)-B_(-q)=2q(1+x)C and B_(+q)+B_(-q)=2B_0 at every grade. The two-branch exterior character therefore contains a forced scalar 2q and degenerates exactly on the reflection-fixed tower q=0. All further q-dependence arises from the relative lattice translations used to assemble a component, not from its local path weights.
